14.6 Tangent Planes and Differentials

In single-variable differential calculus we saw how the derivative defined the tangent line to the graph of a differentiable function at a point on the graph. The tangent line then provided for a linearization of the function at the point. In this section, we will see analogously how the gradient defines the tangent plane to the level surface of a function w = ƒ(x, y, z) at a point on the surface. In the same way as before, the tangent plane then provides for a linear- ization of ƒ at the point and defines the total differential of the function.
